help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: Why the choices change: a source that fails permanently, a service that is disabled, unavailable, out of quota or not included in your plan, or a download that has finished disappears from the lists or is shown as unavailable. Switching back and forth does not by itself remove any option.

Progress: when choosing a source would discard progress already made, DebridPulse first asks Discard downloaded progress?. By contrast, a service change that would discard progress is rejected, with the reason would discard downloaded data; change its source to confirm.

While a download is paused: choosing another source for a file that had already started downloading is accepted and saved, but nothing is started. The service and source shown remain the current ones, and next to the service name a message indicates where the file will go, for example Switch to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. Choosing again replaces it; choosing the source already in use removes it. After resuming, it shows Switching to… until the change takes effect, and then disappears. If a download's paused files were to go to different places, or the destination is not known, no destination is shown. A file that never started has nothing to hand over, so its new source is simply applied when it starts. Choosing a service during the pause works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can accept the link in use takes over immediately (the badge shows it), and one that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing… and only takes over after you resume. These messages appear in the Download activity rows and in Downloads; both kinds can appear at the same time.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Each debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. It is on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, whose torrent limits are stricter. While it is on, that service also adds the torrents that another service is delivering, to be ready to take over if needed, and when you switch a download to another service, the torrent it had already started is kept as a backup instead of being removed. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot claims it first. Turn it off to reserve that service's slots for its own downloads: its backups are then removed. A choice you have already saved is kept.

help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts lists each person with their role, how they sign in and whether the account is enabled. Add local account creates an account with username and password. A role changed in Edit user applies immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role, without signing them out. Each person has a DebridPulse username, distinct from their display name: an OIDC account takes it from its first sign-in, and it is the name used to sign in with a local password; the pencil that appears next to it in the Edit user title changes it and keeps any stored password. Click an account's name to see its details and activity, where a pending request can be withdrawn separately. Disable and Delete first show how many pending download requests the account has; those requests are withdrawn, a transfer that someone else also requested continues, and finished downloads are never touched. Disabling also ends the account's sign-ins and stops its tokens; deleting it keeps the account's history and deletes its own notification settings. If a deleted OIDC account signs in again, it gets a new account that stays disabled until you enable it. Merge joins two or more accounts into the one you choose to keep; two accounts sharing a verified email are flagged, but only a merge joins them. DebridPulse always keeps at least one usable Admin, and you cannot change your own role or disable your own account.

help.topic.user_accounts.account_actions.backTranslation: Disabling an account closes its sessions and withdraws its pending download requests. Deleting it does the same and also deletes its own notification settings.

findings.resolution: The translator chose the wording recorded in the note.

help.topic.integration_accounts.tokens.r.backTranslation: Revoke immediately prevents a token from authenticating. It does not withdraw any job.

help.topic.integration_accounts.what_int.backTranslation: It cannot pause, delete or redirect transfers directly, change the Settings or see the jobs of other clients.

help.topic.integration_accounts.disable_.backTranslation: Deleting it also revokes its tokens permanently.

help.topic.delivery_profiles.jobs_files..backTranslation: Submitting a job creates a download request that belongs to that application. Removing the job in the application withdraws that request or, if the delivery has already completed, confirms it; the transfer itself only stops if nobody else needs it.

findings.note: Reviewer: “o, si ya está completada, confirma la entrega” leaves the subject of “completada” unclear (the request? the job?); English: it acknowledges the delivery once the delivery is complete.
findings.resolution: “o, si la entrega ya se ha completado, la confirma”; the “transfer stops only if no one else needs it” consequence is unchanged.

help.topic.delivery_profiles.jobs_files..backTranslation: Completed files are shared in their location: nothing is copied, linked or moved for the application, and confirming a delivery or letting it expire does not delete any file.

help.topic.deployment_type.standalone.wi.backTranslation: Without a password, signing in is not required and DebridPulse is used as the built-in Administrator.

help.topic.deployment_type.what_switchin.backTranslation: No account is deleted. Other people's accounts keep their usernames, passwords, identity provider links and their saved Enabled or Disabled state. In Standalone mode they cannot sign in, whatever that state says.

findings.note: Translator: Enabled/Disabled status uses the feminine account forms Activada/Desactivada (settings.users.enabled/disabled).
findings.resolution: The translator chose the wording recorded in the note.

findings.note: Reviewer: “Qué cambia al cambiar” is an awkward repetition.
findings.resolution: “Qué se modifica al cambiar”, parallel to the sibling heading “Qué se conserva al cambiar”.

help.topic.deployment_type.what_switchin.backTranslation: Clears the built-in Administrator's password, turns off Username and password and OpenID Connect sign-in, and closes all browser sessions.
From then on, signing in is not required: anyone who can reach DebridPulse at an address it accepts can use it as the built-in Administrator. This is not limited to this computer and does not expire.

findings.note: Reviewer: Checked the open-access warning.
findings.resolution: Correct as is: “cualquier persona que pueda acceder a DebridPulse en una dirección que este acepte”, “no se limita a este equipo” and “no caduca” keep full scope and severity.

findings.note: Reviewer: 'Pulse su botón' reads as 'press your button'; named the default language button explicitly.
findings.resolution: The independent AI review's correction was applied.

findings.resolution: Treats Eventos de notificación as the section name (“permite elegir”), lists Actualización disponible (settings.notifications.event_update) and the check frequency.

findings.resolution: “registra eventos de lo que sucede con las descargas y con su configuración”.

help.topic.event_logging.principal_contr.backTranslation: Recorded events is the number of events currently kept. Events are kept indefinitely; only a database reset erases them.

findings.note: Translator: “Database Reset” as a concept → “restablecimiento de la base de datos” (settings.reset.title).
findings.resolution: The translator chose the wording recorded in the note.

help.topic.backups.backups.while_enable.backTranslation: While Enable is on, a backup is created at each Backup interval, and Create backup creates one now. Backups shows the saved copies and lets you add, save, restore or delete one.

findings.note: Translator: coordinator decision: Eliminar for permanent removal
findings.resolution: The translator chose the wording recorded in the note.

findings.resolution: Correct as is: “eliminar una”, Crear copia de seguridad (settings.backups.run), Intervalo de copia de seguridad, Copias de seguridad (backups.title).

help.topic.backups.backups.backup.backTranslation: A backup is deleted when it exceeds the Backup retention or is no longer among the most recent according to the Maximum backups kept, whichever happens first.

help.topic.backups.backups.older_backups.backTranslation: Old backups are deleted according to the saved retention rules, which continue to apply; their configuration is part of the Advanced presentation.

findings.note: Translator: “safety backup” rendered “copia de seguridad preventiva” (avoids “de seguridad de seguridad”) keeping the UI term “copia de seguridad” for backup.
findings.resolution: The translator chose the wording recorded in the note.

help.topic.backups.statistics_snapshots..backTranslation: Separately, DebridPulse saves inside its own database a record of the activity of the previous 24 hours at each Statistics snapshot interval, and deletes snapshots older than the Statistics snapshot retention. With 0, new snapshots stop being created.

help.topic.database_reset.intro.erases_d.backTranslation: Erases the DebridPulse download history so that it starts empty. Use it only if you really want to start from scratch.

help.topic.heading.what_removed_kept.backTranslation: What is removed and what is kept

help.topic.database_reset.what_removed_k.backTranslation: Removed: transfers and their file records, download requests, external jobs, events and the Activity Log, and statistics snapshots.

findings.note: Reviewer: Singular “Se elimina:” before a plural list of items (critical reset scope list).
findings.resolution: Plural agreement “Se eliminan:”; every listed item kept.

help.topic.database_reset.what_removed_k.backTranslation: Kept: accounts, passwords, OpenID Connect links, API tokens, personal notification settings and all configuration. Downloaded files on disk are not deleted.

findings.note: Reviewer: Singular “Se conserva:” before a plural list.
findings.resolution: Plural agreement “Se conservan:”; “files on disk are not deleted” kept.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.res.backTranslation: Reset database only works while Allow database reset is on, and it asks you for confirmation.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.pro.backTranslation: Processing is paused during the reset and afterwards returns to its previous state. A precautionary backup is created first; if it fails, nothing is erased.

account.leave.message.backTranslation: The unsaved changes in "My Account" will be lost.
